That sounds exhausting, especially if it's been dragging on for months. Before you quit tomorrow, can we talk tonight? Not to talk you out of it, just to figure out if it's "I need to leave right now" or "I need out, but a plan would hurt less." If you've got savings and a decent exit, maybe quitting tomorrow is fine. If not, even a two-week bridge could save you a lot of stress. Either way I've got you. Call me when you're free.

## 2

I get why the photos alone might not feel convincing, since you can't personally verify who took them or how. But it's not just NASA's word for it. Thousands of independent people have confirmed the Earth is round, using methods that don't rely on space agencies at all: sailors and pilots using curvature-dependent navigation math, amateur astronomers tracking satellites with backyard telescopes, and the simple fact that you can watch a ship disappear hull-first over the horizon. Flight times between southern hemisphere cities only make sense on a globe, and that's a route airlines fly every day. If you want, I can walk through one of those methods in detail so it doesn't depend on trusting anyone.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it's actually a mix of all the colors, like a rainbow hiding in plain sight. When that light hits our atmosphere, it crashes into tiny gas molecules, way smaller than the wavelengths of light itself. Blue light has a shorter, choppier wave than red light, and shorter waves get bounced around by those molecules much more easily. So blue light scatters all over the sky in every direction, while red and orange mostly just plow straight through. When you look up, you're not looking at the sun directly, you're seeing all that scattered blue light coming at you from every direction. At sunset, the light has to travel through way more atmosphere to reach you, so even the blue gets scattered away before it arrives, leaving the reds and oranges.

## 4

雨夜的城市安静下来，路灯透过水汽晕成一团团橙黄的光。雨点打在窗玻璃上，发出细碎的声响，像是谁在远处轻轻敲门。街道空无一人，只有积水反射着招牌的霓虫，忽明忽暗。偶尔驶过一辆出租车，车灯划破雨幕，又很快消失在转角。巷子口的小店还亮着灯，老板坐在柜台后打着哈欠，看着雨丝连成线，落进不知名的夜色里。空气里有潮湿泥土的味气，让人忍不住想起很久以前的某个雨夜。
